QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_2

question.text: A mutual fund scheme has delivered a return of 14% with a standard deviation of 4%. If the risk-free rate is 5%, what is the Sharpe Ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Sharpe Ratio = (Investment Return - Risk-free Rate) / Standard Deviation = (14% - 5%) / 4% = 9% / 4% = 2.25. Among comparable schemes, the higher Sharpe denotes higher return per unit of total risk. The Trap: Option B (3.50) divides total return (14%) by SD (4%) without subtracting the risk-free rate. Option C (0.44) reverses the ratio. Option D (9.00) reports only the excess return (14% - 5% = 9%) without dividing by SD. Note: Distributor coaching wording removed; final paragraph recast in neutral Retirement Adviser terms using the higher-return-per-unit-of-risk interpretation.
